title: Robust Device-Independent Certification of Boolean-Phase Gates
authors: Yunguang Han, Xingyuan Bu, Aleksandra Gočanin, Jiabing Yuan
abstract: Device-independent certification of a quantum gate requires the input and output tests to identify the same reference qubits. Self-testing the output Choi state alone does not guarantee this consistency. We develop a robust certification scheme for Boolean-phase gates, a broad family of computational-basis diagonal gates specified by Boolean functions. Boolean derivatives convert the target-dependent phase information into classical signs that can be evaluated from local measurement outcomes. This leads to Bell tests built from CHSH blocks using two binary measurements per party and no entangling measurements. At maximal violation, the tests self-test the normalized Choi state and the measured observables. Away from the maximum, they give an explicit affine lower bound on the extracted-state squared fidelity that is uniform over all Boolean functions and valid in arbitrary local dimensions. We then combine an identity test and a gate-output test in an independent-source network in which the reference devices use the same physical observables, obtaining a closed-form Choi-fidelity bound for an effective \(n\)-qubit channel. For CCZ, a joint six-party analysis gives a stronger robustness bound without changing the Bell expression or measurement settings. The construction shows how the algebraic structure of a gate can shift target-dependent information from quantum measurement design to classical processing of local outcomes.
summary: This paper presents a robust, device-independent method to certify the fidelity of Boolean-phase quantum gates. It achieves this by transforming the gate's phase dependence into classical constraints evaluated via Bell inequalities using only local measurements. The resulting fidelity bound is explicit and uniform over all Boolean functions, providing a powerful tool for quantum device characterization.
main_problem: The paper develops a robust, device-independent certification scheme for Boolean-phase gates, addressing the issue that self-testing the output Choi state alone is insufficient.
main_result: They derive a closed-form Choi-fidelity bound for an effective n-qubit channel by combining an identity test and a gate-output test in an independent-source network.
method: The core method involves using Boolean differentiation to convert gate-dependent phase information into classical signs, which are then evaluated using Bell tests built from CHSH blocks with only local measurements.
model_or_system: The system under study is the Boolean-phase gate, defined by a Boolean function f on n qubits, represented as a diagonal unitary matrix. The certification is performed using an independent-source network structure.
key_observables: The normalized Choi state, the Bell expression $B_f$, and the extracted-state squared fidelity $F^2(ho_{	ext{ext}}, |\Psi_fangle\langle\Psi_f|)$.
important_parameters: The Bell deficit $\epsilon$, which quantifies the deviation from maximal violation, and the number of qubits $n$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to combine an identity test and a gate-output test using the same physical observables, and that the B-side extraction preserves every physical Z-measurement exactly.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the Boolean-derivative scoring for a Bell term, mapping outcomes to bits and the derivative sign. Figure 2 illustrates the independent-source network structure used for the combined test.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem and the Boolean-derivative technique. It then establishes self-testing bounds (Theorem 1) and derives a robust fidelity bound (Theorem 2) using an independent-source network. Finally, it applies this framework to the CCZ gate using a joint six-party analysis.
why_interesting: The technique of translating gate-specific quantum information into classical constraints on local measurements is highly generalizable and provides a powerful tool for verifying quantum hardware fidelity in a resource-efficient manner.

The upper curves show the squared Choi-state fidelity obtained from a single state test, while the lower curves show the squared Choi fidelity of the effective channel obtained by composing the input and output certificates. Dashed curves use the uniform coefficient cZ, and solid curves use the im- proved CCZ coefficient cCCZ.
